body:
22 Nov 2026, P2-25 SLICE 4, PR #118, SECOND FIX ROUND (built, not walked, not deployed; P2-25 stays todo; B-46 is N-46). Code at 6605946. The adversarial tester proved no loss of a like, a file or a mapping; its permanent-defect and false-text items are closed at the source, each probe rebuilt as a permanent test seen RED on 12a232a (its files and seed 7073 are gone: the rates below are my own generator's).

ROOT (proved on seeded random worlds): a decision of the pass read state that the same pass changes. FIX: (1) PROBE 6: "another file" is a file the listing of THIS pass leaves alive (link_listing.Listing.alive, the test scanner._prune removes by). page() only NOTES tags; the rehome decides after the whole listing + scan + prune, so an incomplete pass writes NOTHING. Costs: a library whose listing never completes is never rehomed; the pass holds the worklist files' tags in memory (330 B a file, 67 MB at 200,000). (2) SEED 7073: a move never writes the length or an id of a song that exists (refs.resolve_keeping_identity, marked STOP-GAP). (3) SECOND-PASS WRITES: a TRUE FIXPOINT, small and bounded: after each round the verdicts a move can change are judged again (the last file of an owned song once a file arrived; a nameless file once a song a move made carries its id; kept or moved files whose tags carry the id of a song a move made: they fit as well as another and the song is held); a file moves at most once so rounds <= files+1, typically 2 (MAX_ROUNDS 25 second layer). The invariant is KEPT: a second pass over an unchanged catalogue writes nothing and takes no copy; the outcome is independent of page size, listing order, a cut by the music server and a KILL between chunks. I TESTED MY OWN CLAIM about the kill and it was false at first (the made song's id made a kept file ambiguous only after the kill); the 1,500-world scan had also found 3 second-pass writes of that cause. Both fixed. (4) PROBE 5: ONE table rehome.HOLDS (reason, what frees it, whether tagging does); the log line and the audit FAIL line are made from it; tagging frees the untagged AND the nameless file, not the other two. (5) TIMING re-measured (3 runs, machine NOT quiet): a chunk of 500 holds the lock a median ~20 ms, at most 0.28 s; ONE transaction 4.7 s; whole release 17 to 19 s (5 s in one; the lead's quiet run 3.9 s). RELEASE_CHUNK pinned at 500 by a test (1,001 rows: 500, 500, 1).

PROOF: 400 worlds on 12a232a: 24 stranded likes, 18 second-pass writes, 22 differing at page size 500, 2 at page size 1, 3 cut-and-resumed; after: 0 of 1,500 on every one of those and on a kill at the 2nd and 3rd move. 58 new tests in 3 files + 1 pin: 46 of the 58 red on 12a232a (8 of the 9 red text tests only by a missing name; the rest by behaviour); 33 of 34 mutants red (the 34th, judging every stay again, is equivalent in outcome). Whole suite 2674 passed, 13 skipped, 1 xfailed; ruff, format, mypy, check_rows, check_order clean. Real DB copy (sha 1d26a5f77d6dbd7a, 11,784,192 bytes, unchanged): 12 kept, 0 moved, only the worklist changes, audit PASS.
RULINGS APPLIED: (a) N-36 note written; (b) prune keeps a listed file it cannot describe: KEPT; (c) RELEASE_CHUNK stays 500; (d) only-the-length-differs: doubt keeps the file, ACCEPTED.
NOT DONE: the walk, any deploy, audit_stack check library on a real stack; the rehome has run only on synthetic data.

LEAD 23 Nov: the fixer stopped on the 5-hour usage limit (21:08 UTC 22 Nov; not a shutdown, not billing) before posting this; the lead posted it from the saved draft. Re-checked at 6605946: the new tests pass, the mutant RELEASE_CHUNK=10**9 is red, ruff, format, mypy, check_rows, check_order clean; one false word fixed (a moved file's contested target stays on the worklist only if it was on it). SUPERSEDES item 5 (timing: 6 ms, 6.65 s) of the 20 Nov 18:15 note.
